## Answer

Using the profile already on file for this exact case — **"Biometric access control for a logistics hub"**: Provider role, risk class **high**, built in Kazakhstan, output used in the EU (EU jurisdiction is marked extraterritorial in the dataset, so the EU AI Act applies here).

## The retention duration

**EU AI Act, Article 19 ("Automatically Generated Logs")** — provider obligation:

> "Providers of high-risk AI systems shall keep the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems, to the extent such logs are under their control. The logs shall be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of **at least six months**, unless provided otherwise in the applicable Union or national law, in particular Union law on the protection of personal data."

So the floor is **6 months**, but the actual required period is "appropriate to the intended purpose" — the Act does not give a fixed number beyond that floor, and it defers to other Union/national law (including data-protection law) which may set something different.

**Effective date: 2 December 2027** for Annex III high-risk systems (biometric access control falls under Annex III, point 1 — Biometrics). As of today, 2026‑09‑19, this obligation is **not yet in force**.

Source: EU AI Act, Art. 19 — official text: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj

## "From when" — the clause is silent

Article 19's text specifies *how long* (≥6 months) but does not state the trigger point the clock runs from (e.g., from each log's creation, from the end of a usage session, from decommissioning of the system). Per the dataset's evidence hint, what's expected in practice is "a retention schedule naming the six-month floor... and the deletion mechanism" — but the statutory text itself does not name a start date. I can't cite a start-of-period rule because none exists in this clause — that silence is the answer, not a gap I can fill from elsewhere.

Related design requirement — **Art. 12(3)**, for biometric identification systems (Annex III 1(a)): logs must capture, at minimum, the **start and end date/time of each use**, the reference database checked, the matched input data, and the identity of the human verifier (Art. 14(5)). These are what get logged, not the retention trigger.

## Unresolved conflict: floor vs. ceiling

The dataset records an **open conflict** (`conf-retention-floor-vs-ceiling`, nature: *quantity*) between this floor and:

**GDPR Art. 5(1)(e)** (Storage limitation), in force since 25 May 2018:

> "Personal data shall be kept in a form which permits identification of data subjects for **no longer than is necessary** for the purposes for which the personal data are processed."

Summary in the dataset: *"AI Act sets a six-month floor for log retention; GDPR sets a necessity ceiling on the same logs."* Since the logs are biometric (personal data) under Art. 12(3), this ceiling is unavoidable here.

**This conflict's resolution status is "open."** There is no `rationale` and no `decidedBy` recorded in the dataset — it has not been decided, and the dataset does not identify who is responsible for resolving it. I won't guess at a resolution or average the two positions: you cannot treat "6 months" as safe-and-sufficient without also independently justifying why 6 months (or whatever longer period you pick for the stated purpose) doesn't exceed what's "necessary" under GDPR — that necessity judgment isn't quantified anywhere in either text.

Source: GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) — official text: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj

---

**Bottom line:** Once Art. 19 takes effect (2 Dec 2027 for this Annex III system), you must keep the logs at least 6 months, for a period matched to the system's intended purpose, with no stated start-of-period trigger — and simultaneously must not keep personal-data logs longer than GDPR's necessity ceiling allows, with no dataset-recorded decision on how those two requirements reconcile.
